[build-system].requires: A list of build-time dependencies required to execute the project's build system. For example, it usually includes setuptools, wheel, poetry-core, hatchling, or other build backend packages.
[project].dynamic: A list of project metadata fields that are intentionally not specified statically in pyproject.toml and will be provided dynamically by the build backend or another tool during the build process.
[project].name: The distribution name of the Python project. This is the package name used in package indexes such as PyPI and in installation commands.
[project].version: The version of the project. It should follow Python packaging version rules and identifies a specific release of the distribution.
[project].requires-python: Specifies the Python version requirement for the project, such as >=3.8 or >=3.10,<4. It tells installers which Python versions are compatible with the package.
[project].authors: Lists the people or organizations considered to be the authors of the project. Each entry can include a name, an email address, or both.
[project].maintainers: Lists the people or organizations responsible for maintaining the project. Its structure is similar to authors and can include name and email fields.
[project].description: A short one-line summary of the project. It is used as the package summary in distribution metadata.
[project].readme: Specifies the project's long description, usually by pointing to a README file such as README.md or README.rst, or by providing text and content type directly.
[project].license: Specifies the project's license. In modern pyproject.toml metadata, this is usually an SPDX license expression such as MIT, Apache-2.0, or BSD-3-Clause.
[project].license-files: Lists license files or legal notice files that should be included in the distribution. The values are glob patterns relative to the project root.
[project].keywords: A list of keywords describing the project. These keywords help classify and search for the package.
[project].classifiers: A list of Trove classifiers describing the project, such as supported Python versions, license, framework, development status, or intended audience.
[project.urls]: A table of project-related URLs. Each key is a label such as Homepage, Repository, Documentation, or Bug Tracker, and each value is the corresponding URL.
[tool.setuptools.py-modules]: A setuptools-specific list of single-file Python modules to include in the distribution. This is used for projects that provide modules like foo.py instead of package directories.
[tool.setuptools.ext-modules]: A setuptools-specific list of extension modules to build, typically for C/C++/Cython extensions. Each entry corresponds to a setuptools.Extension configuration. This field is marked experimental in setuptools documentation.
[tool.setuptools.packages]: Controls which Python packages are included in the distribution. It can explicitly list package names or use a find directive to automatically discover packages.
[tool.setuptools.package-dir]: Maps package names to source directories. It is commonly used for src-layout projects, for example mapping the root package namespace to the src directory.
[tool.setuptools.package-data]: Specifies non-Python data files that should be included inside package directories, such as JSON files, templates, type stubs, or resource files.
[tool.setuptools.exclude-package-data]: Specifies package data files that should be excluded from the distribution, even if they would otherwise be included.
[tool.setuptools.license-files]: A setuptools-specific field for including license files using glob patterns. It is deprecated in favor of the standard [project].license-files field.
[tool.setuptools.data-files]: Specifies data files to install outside package directories. This field is discouraged because files outside package directories are harder to manage portably.
[tool.setuptools.provides]: A legacy metadata field listing packages or features provided by this distribution. Setuptools documentation notes that pip ignores this field when installing packages.
[tool.setuptools.obsoletes]: A legacy metadata field listing packages or distributions that this project obsoletes. Setuptools documentation notes that pip ignores this field when installing packages.
[tool.setuptools.platforms]: Specifies platform information for the distribution and maps to the Platform core metadata field. It is mostly informational and is ignored by pip during installation.
[tool.setuptools.zip-safe]: A legacy/obsolete setuptools flag indicating whether the project can be safely installed and run as a zipped egg. It is mainly relevant to deprecated egg/easy_install workflows.
[tool.setuptools.eager-resources]: An obsolete setuptools field related to resources that should be extracted early when using eggs and pkg_resources. It is mainly relevant to deprecated egg/easy_install workflows.
[tool.setuptools.namespace-packages]: A deprecated setuptools field for declaring namespace packages. Modern projects should use implicit namespace packages defined by PEP 420 instead.
[dependency-groups]: Defines named groups of dependencies in pyproject.toml. These groups are mainly intended for development-related dependencies such as testing, linting, documentation, or local tooling, and they are not included as package metadata when the project is built.
[project].dependencies: Defines the project's required runtime dependencies. The value is an array of PEP 508 dependency strings, and each dependency is installed when users install the package.
[project.optional-dependencies]: Defines optional dependency groups, also known as extras. Each key is an extra name, and each value is an array of PEP 508 dependency strings that are installed only when that extra is requested.
[tool.poetry.dependencies]: Defines the main dependencies used by Poetry. These are the dependencies required by the project at runtime. In Poetry 2.0 and later, project.dependencies is preferred for standard package metadata, while tool.poetry.dependencies is still used for Poetry-specific dependency information and locking behavior.
[tool.poetry.dev-dependencies]: A legacy Poetry section for development dependencies. It was commonly used for packages needed during development, testing, or tooling, but modern Poetry projects should use dependency groups such as [dependency-groups] or [tool.poetry.group.dev.dependencies] instead.
[[tool.poetry.source]].url: Defines the URL of a package source used by Poetry, such as a private package index or an alternative repository. Dependencies can later refer to this source by name.
[build-system].build-backend: Specifies the Python build backend that the build frontend should import and call to build the project, such as setuptools.build_meta, poetry.core.masonry.api, hatchling.build, or flit_core.buildapi.
[build-system].backend-path: Specifies one or more local directories inside the source tree that should be added to sys.path when loading an in-tree build backend. It is used when the build backend code is shipped inside the project itself.
[project].scripts: Defines console command entry points for the package. Each key is the command name that will be installed, and each value is a Python object reference such as package.module:function. This is the standard pyproject.toml replacement for console_scripts.
[project].entry-points.'console_scripts': This should generally not be used in standard pyproject.toml metadata. The console_scripts entry point group is represented by [project.scripts]. Defining [project.entry-points.console_scripts] is considered ambiguous and build backends are expected to reject it.
[tool.setuptools.script-files]: A setuptools-specific field listing script files to install. It is discouraged because it corresponds to the older setup.py script keyword; project.scripts should be used instead when possible.
[tool.poetry.scripts]: Defines scripts or executables installed by Poetry-built packages. For console scripts, Poetry now recommends using [project.scripts]. [tool.poetry.scripts] is mainly retained for Poetry-specific script handling, especially file-type scripts.
[project].entry-points.'plugins': Defines a custom entry point group named plugins under the standard [project.entry-points] table. Each key is a plugin name, and each value is a Python object reference. This allows other tools or frameworks to discover plugin implementations through package metadata.
[tool.poetry.plugins]: Defines Poetry-style plugin entry points. Each subtable name represents a plugin group, and each key-value pair maps a plugin name to a Python module object reference, such as package.module:ClassName or package.module:function.
[tool.pytest]: Native TOML configuration section for pytest.
[tool.pytest.ini_options]: INI-style pytest configuration section stored inside pyproject.toml.
[tool.pytest.ini_options].minversion: Specifies the minimum pytest version required by the project.
[tool.pytest.ini_options].addopts: Defines default command-line options passed to pytest.
[tool.pytest.ini_options].testpaths: Lists directories where pytest should look for tests.
[tool.pytest.ini_options].python_files: Specifies filename patterns that pytest treats as test files.
[tool.pytest.ini_options].python_classes: Specifies class-name patterns that pytest treats as test classes.
[tool.pytest.ini_options].python_functio: Specifies function-name patterns that pytest treats as test functions.
[tool.pytest.ini_options].markers: Registers custom pytest markers used by the test suite.
[tool.pytest.ini_options].log_cli: Controls whether pytest displays live log output during test execution.
[tool.pytest.ini_options].xfail_strict: Controls whether unexpected passes for xfail tests should be treated as failures.
[tool.poetry].keywords: Poetry-specific project keywords. Deprecated in favor of [project].keywords.
[tool.poetry].classifiers: Poetry-specific Trove classifiers. In modern projects, [project].classifiers is the standard metadata field.
[tool.poetry].package-mode: Controls whether Poetry treats the project as a package. If set to false, Poetry can manage dependencies without building/installing the current project as a package.
[tool.poetry].name: Poetry-specific project name field. In modern Poetry projects, [project].name is preferred, but this field may still appear in Poetry configurations.
[tool.poetry].version: Poetry-specific project version field. In modern Poetry projects, [project].version is preferred unless Poetry-specific dynamic version handling is needed.
[tool.poetry].description: Poetry-specific short project description. Deprecated in favor of [project].description.
[tool.poetry].license: Poetry-specific license field. Deprecated in favor of [project].license.
[tool.poetry].authors: Poetry-specific author list. Deprecated in favor of [project].authors.
[tool.poetry].maintainers: Poetry-specific maintainer list. Deprecated in favor of [project].maintainers.
[tool.poetry].readme: Poetry-specific README field. It can point to one README file or multiple README files.
[tool.poetry].homepage: Poetry-specific homepage URL. Deprecated in favor of [project.urls].
[tool.poetry].repository: Poetry-specific source repository URL. Deprecated in favor of [project.urls].
[tool.poetry].documentation: Poetry-specific documentation URL. Deprecated in favor of [project.urls].
[tool.poetry].keywords: Poetry-specific project keywords. Deprecated in favor of [project].keywords.
[tool.poetry].classifiers: Poetry-specific Trove classifiers. In modern projects, [project].classifiers is the standard metadata field.
[tool.poetry].packages: Controls which packages or modules Poetry includes in the built distribution. It can specify include paths, source directories, target paths, and build formats.
[tool.poetry].include: Specifies additional files or glob patterns that Poetry should include in distribution artifacts.
[tool.poetry].exclude: Specifies files or glob patterns that Poetry should exclude from distribution artifacts.
